title: Archive staging and transfer manifest
software_contract: review_archive(request) validates the entire input before producing a proposal; invalid input raises ValueError (message unspecified) and input is not mutated. Each item is indivisible and may be selected at most once. Choose items whose total size is at most capacity and whose total priority is greatest. Among equal-priority feasible selections choose the lexicographically smallest tuple of selected zero-based input indices (ordinary Python tuple order), not the smallest item count, smallest used space, or least change from current. Empty selection is valid and wins when all attainable priorities are zero. Return item_count, capacity, current, proposed, changes and manifest. current and proposed each contain selected IDs in item input order, used (sum of sizes), priority (sum of priorities), feasible (used <= capacity), remaining_capacity (capacity-used). The current selection may exceed capacity and must still be assessed; negative remaining capacity is then reported. changes.add and changes.remove list IDs in item input order. manifest contains proposed items in input order, each with item_id, offset (sum of preceding proposed sizes, starting at zero) and length (item size). This is a transfer plan only; no files are read or written. Exact greatest priority and the stated tie rule are required. CLI reads a JSON request and prints a report; invalid input has nonzero exit and no successful report.
input_domain: Object with exactly items (finite list), current (finite list) and capacity (nonnegative Python int, not bool). Each item has exactly item_id (unique nonempty string), size (positive Python int, not bool), priority (nonnegative Python int, not bool). current contains distinct known item IDs in any order; it need not fit capacity. Empty lists and zero capacity are valid. No artificial item-count or integer bound; priorities are additive abstract importance units, not probabilities. There is no mandatory item or secondary minimum-change objective.
execution_assumptions: Item sizes and available capacity use the same integer unit; priorities are supplied by the caller. The program does not infer their business validity.
No hardware, resource budget, latency target or benefit measurement is provided.
